trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive 1 mile to Westside Road and turn left (north). Follow it to the barricade at Dry Creek and park in the small lot south of it; the road beyond is closed to vehicles.
approach: From Westside Road — Dry Creek Trailhead, walk the closed road past the barricade to the Tahoma Creek Trail and climb it about 2 miles to the Wonderland Trail junction near 4300 ft. Go south over the Tahoma Creek suspension bridge, follow the Wonderland Trail to Indian Henry's Hunting Ground, then take the Mirror Lakes Trail until it fades in the basin between Copper and Pyramid Peaks. Continue cross-country past Pyramid Peak to Success Cleaver and climb it to about 8000 ft, where glacier travel begins. A roped traverse across the South Tahoma Glacier at roughly 8100 ft reaches the base of Tahoma Cleaver.
note: 'gain about 8000 ft' was wrong (8000 ft is an elevation where glacier travel starts); dropped 'currently'. Approach is the Glacier Island traverse line, the only page found reaching Tahoma Cleaver; no page describes Tahoma Cleaver itself.

trailheadDirection: From US-2 at Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive south 4.2 miles to the Snow Lakes trailhead parking lot.
approach: From the Snow Lakes Trailhead, follow the Snow Lakes Trail past the footbridge about 4 miles in and on to Nada Lake. The ridge lies high above the lake; the way up leaves the lake at the gully that drains Temple Canyon and Tamarack Meadows. Steep terrain in that gully eases near 5800 ft, and from there the summit is about one mile and 2000 ft of climbing away.
note: Drive confirmed by WTA. Removed the mossy-slot claim (a snow-covered winter detail, unsafe as summer advice); footbridge 4 mi from a single winter report only; evidence is one trip report, so low confidence.
